ACT XLVII OF 1975
ACT XLVII OF 1975
PAKISTAN INSURANCE
CORPORATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1975
An Act further to
amend the Pakistan Insurance Corporation Act, 1952
[Gazette of
Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 29th April 1975]
The following Act of Parliament
received the assent of the President on the 25th April 1975, and is hereby
published for general information:-
1. Short title and
commencement.----(1) This Act may be called the Pakistan Insurance
Corporation (Amendment) Act, 1975.
(2) It shall come into force at
once.

4. Amendment of section 4-A,
Act XXXVIII of 1952.-In the said Act, in section 4-A, for subsection (1)
the following shall be substituted, namely:-
" (1) The Corporation shall
maintain two separate registers of share holders as follows:-
(a) one at Lahore to be called
the Lahore Register for the areas com prising the Punjab, the North-West
Frontier Province and the Federal Capital; and
(b) the other at Karachi to be
called the Karachi Register for the areas comprising Baluchistan and Sind and
places not falling within the area referred to in clause (a).".

Insertion of new section 29-B, Act XXXVIII of 1952

ACT XLVII OF 1975
ACT XLVII OF 1975
PAKISTAN INSURANCE
CORPORATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1975
An Act further to
amend the Pakistan Insurance Corporation Act, 1952
[Gazette of
Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 29th April 1975]
The following Act of Parliament
received the assent of the President on the 25th April 1975, and is hereby
published for general information:-
8. Insertion of new section
29-B, Act XXXVIII of 1952.-In the said Act, after section 29-A, the
following new section shall be inserted namely:-
"29-B. Power to call for and
examine accounts, etc.-(1) For the purpose of satisfying itself that provisions
of this Act have been or are being duly complied with, or for verifying the
correctness of the claims, declarations, returns, statements, or other
information submitted to it, the Corporation may, whenever it may consider
necessary, call for or examine or cause to be examined any accounts books,
documents, memoranda or other records of any insurer or his agent.
(2) Every insurer or his agent
shall, when called upon to do so under subsection (1), produce and make freely
accessible to the Corporation or to its representative duly appointed in this
behalf such accounts books, documents, memoranda or other records as are or
should normally be in his prossession or control, and shall otherwise
facilitate the examination thereof.
(3) Whoever wilfully obstructs
the Corporation or any person authorised by it in the exercise of its or his
powers or performance of functions under subsection (1) or subsection (2), or
fails without reasonable cause to comply with a request made thereunder, shall,
in respect of each occasion on which any such obstruction or failure takes
place, be punishable with fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees".
sections.punishment: punishable with fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees".
